Encyclopaedia Britannica's editors oversee subject areas in which they have extensive knowledge, whether from years of experience gained by working on that content or via study for an advanced degree. **Volkswagen Group**, major German automobile manufacturer, founded by the German government in 1937 to mass-produce a low-priced “people’s car.” Headquarters are in Wolfsburg, Germany. The Austrian automotive engineer Ferdinand Porsche, who was responsible for the original design of the car, was hired by the German Labour Front in 1934, and ground was broken for a new factory in the state of Lower Saxony in 1938. Control of the company was transferred in 1949 to the West German government and the state of Lower Saxony. Joint ownership of Volkswagen by the West German government and the state of Lower Saxony continued until 1960, when the company was mostly denationalized with the sale of 60 percent of its stock to the public.

title: Volkswagen - Wikipedia
content: # Volkswagen. **Volkswagen AG** (German pronunciation:  ⓘ), commonly abbreviated to **VW**, is a German automobile manufacturer based in Wolfsburg, Lower Saxony, Germany. Established in 1937 by the German Labour Front, it was revived after World War II by British Army officer Ivan Hirst and, over the 81 years since, grew into the global brand it is today. As of 2025, the company had a market capitalization of approximately US$58.9 billion. The company is well known for the Beetle and serves as the flagship brand of its eponymous conglomerate "Conglomerate (company)"), the Volkswagen Group, which was the world's largest automotive manufacturer by global sales in 2016 and 2017. content: The company has shifted its focus toward electric vehicles, with plans to introduce multiple new electric models by 2026, aiming for 70% of its sales in Europe to be electric. Volkswagen AG, commonly known as Volkswagen or VW, is a prominent German automotive manufacturer headquartered in Wolfsburg, Lower Saxony. Founded on May 28, 1937, by the German Labour Front, the company was initially established to produce an affordable "people's car" as envisioned by Adolf Hitler. Over the decades, Volkswagen expanded its portfolio by acquiring various luxury brands, including Audi, Porsche, Bentley, and Lamborghini, which helped solidify its position as one of the largest automakers globally.
